newsitem.title: Australia: Rugby union-Murdoch joins injury-hit Wallabies.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Murdoch joins injury-hit Wallabies.

text.p: New South Wales winger Alistair Murdoch has become the latest player to be drafted into Australia's injury-hit rugby union tour of Europe, the Australian Rugby Union (ARU) said on Thursday.

An ARU spokesman told reporters Murdoch would replace Australian Capital Territory (ACT) centre Adam Magro, who broke a bone in his left foot in the final minutes of Wednesday's 25-9 defeat of Scottish Districts. Murdoch will leave for Scotland on Friday.
The match against Scottish Districts was Magro's first since he was called into the Wallaby squad as a back-up for injured Queensland centre Jason Little.
Murdoch, who has played two tests for Australia, leaves on Friday to join the Wallabies ahead of Saturday's test against Scotland.

Australia selectors had to overlook seven injured players when choosing their line-up for the Scotland test. The injured players are forwards Michael Brial, Mark Connors, John Welborn, Brett Robinson and David Giffin and backs Little and Magro.
New South Wales lock Warwick Waugh was the first player to be drafted into the side when Garrick Morgan suffered a broken ankle in the opening match of the tour.
New South Wales captain Tim Gavin was then called on to replace Connors before Magro flew to Europe with ACT backrower Owen Finegan, who had been called in as Brial's replacement.
